heard: A radio blast lasted the exact duration the telescope could watch. On August 15, 1977, Ohio State University's Big Ear Telescope picked up the powerful anomaly. Astronomer Jerry R. Amen discovered the signal while reviewing computer printout data. Amen circled the intensity reading 6EQJ5 and wrote while beside it. The signal frequency hit around 1420 MHz, matching the neutral hydrogen emission line. A recent 2024 study proposed a magnetar flare energized a cold hydrogen cloud to create it. Despite decades of searches, the mysterious anomaly from the constellation Sagittarius has never recurred. That exactly matches a radio blast that lasted the exact duration the telescope could watch.
